name: EP-14 SaaS Subscription Billing (Backlog)
w: How hostel owners pay for Hostel ERP. Today anyone can sign up and use everything for free, with no plans, limits or billing. This epic adds plans and pricing, a free trial, recurring payment through a gateway, GST invoices from the business to its customers, and a fair path when a customer stops paying that never deletes their data. Prices themselves are a business decision for the owner; the system makes them configurable.

E14-T2 Subscriptions per owner account
E14-T3 Free trial at sign-up
E14-T4 Enforce plan limits

out: No usage-based metering beyond bed count, no reseller or partner billing, no invoicing of residents (EP-13).
dod: Not started. Each task has its own acceptance criteria. A customer who stops paying never loses data, and gateway webhooks are verified and idempotent with tests.

name: Plans, pricing and limits
w: Everything else in billing depends on knowing what is sold. Hostel software in India is usually priced per bed or per hostel per month; the model must be configurable without code changes.
ac: A plans table: name, price per month and per year in paise, pricing basis (flat, per bed or tiered by beds), and limits (beds, hostels, staff accounts) plus feature flags
Plans are managed by platform admins only; changing a price never changes an existing subscription until renewal
Starting plans and prices are agreed with the owner and recorded in docs/pricing.md before build
Prices are shown including or excluding GST consistently, stated on every price

name: Subscriptions per owner account
w: The paying customer is the owner, who may run several hostels. One subscription per owner covers their hostels, with a clear status that the rest of the app can rely on.
ac: subscriptions: owner, plan, status (trialing, active, past_due, read_only, cancelled), current period start and end, beds counted at renewal, gateway customer and subscription ids
Status changes only through database functions called by webhooks, admins (E10-T7) or scheduled jobs; every change is logged
A private.account_can_write(owner) helper exposes whether the account may write data, used by E14-T9
Every existing owner is migrated onto a plan (for example a grandfathered free plan) so nothing breaks on release

name: Free trial at sign-up
w: A trial lets an owner set up rooms and residents and see the value before paying, without asking for a card at sign-up.
ac: A new owner starts a trial of a configurable length (for example 14 days) with full features
The app shell shows days left and a 'Choose a plan' link during the trial
Reminder emails 7 days, 3 days and 1 day before the trial ends
When the trial ends without a plan, the account moves to read-only (E14-T9), not deleted

name: Enforce plan limits
w: Limits only matter if the database enforces them; the UI alone can be bypassed.
ac: Creating beds, hostels or staff beyond the plan's limits is refused by the database with a clear message naming the limit
Owners see usage against limits in settings and a warning at 80% of a limit
Downgrading below current usage is refused with what needs to be removed first
Existing data above a limit is never deleted or hidden

name: Recurring payments through a gateway
w: Collecting every month by hand does not scale. A gateway with recurring payments (cards and UPI AutoPay) charges automatically, within RBI e-mandate rules.
ac: Choose a gateway with subscriptions and UPI AutoPay (Razorpay or Cashfree) and document why
Owners subscribe through the gateway's hosted checkout; no card or UPI details touch our servers
Signed webhooks update the subscription idempotently (events are de-duplicated by id) for activated, charged, failed, halted and cancelled
RBI e-mandate rules are respected: pre-debit notification is sent by the gateway, and charges above the e-mandate limit need the customer's authentication
A sandbox end-to-end test runs subscribe, renew, fail and cancel

name: GST invoices from the business to hostels
w: Business customers need a proper GST invoice for every charge to claim input tax credit, and the business must issue them to stay compliant.
ac: Every successful charge produces a tax invoice from the business: the business's legal name, address and GSTIN, sequential number per financial year, SAC for software services, taxable value and GST (CGST and SGST, or IGST by place of supply)
Owners can enter their business name and GSTIN so the invoice is B2B
Invoices are immutable, downloadable as PDF and emailed; credit notes handle refunds
Rates, SAC code and place-of-supply rules are confirmed with a chartered accountant before release

name: Failed payments, grace period and dunning
w: Cards expire and mandates fail. Customers should get several chances and clear warnings before anything changes, and nothing should happen silently.
ac: After a failed charge the subscription is past_due; the gateway retries on its schedule
Emails go out on failure, before the grace period ends and when it ends, each with a link to update the payment method
After a configurable grace period (for example 7 days) the account becomes read-only (E14-T9); after a longer period it can be suspended by an admin (E10-T6)
Paying at any point restores full access immediately

name: Billing page for owners
w: Owners need one place to see what they pay, change it and get their invoices, without contacting support.
ac: Shows the current plan, status, usage against limits, next charge date and amount
Upgrade takes effect immediately with proration; downgrade takes effect at the next renewal
Update payment method, download every invoice, cancel with a reason (effective at period end)
Only owners see billing; staff never do

name: Read-only mode for unpaid accounts
w: Cutting a hostel off completely would stop it working mid-month and hold its records hostage. Read-only keeps the owner's data visible and exportable while making payment necessary to keep working.
ac: When an account cannot write, every tenant write (rooms, residents, allocations, invoices, payments) is refused by the database via private.account_can_write, with a message that links to billing
Reads, printing and data export keep working
The app shell shows a clear banner explaining why and how to restore access
Integration tests cover each table's writes in read-only mode

name: Coupons and annual billing
w: Annual plans improve cash flow, and launch discounts help the first customers sign up.
ac: Plans have an annual price; owners can switch between monthly and annual at renewal
Admins create coupons (percentage or fixed, duration, redemption limit, expiry); each coupon redemption is recorded
Coupons are applied through the gateway so its invoices match ours

name: Legal pages the gateway requires
w: Indian payment gateways activate live payments only for sites with terms, privacy, refund and contact pages. They are also needed for the DPDP Act notice.
ac: Public pages for terms of service, privacy policy, refund and cancellation policy, and contact details, linked from sign-up and the footer
Sign-up records acceptance of the terms version
Texts are reviewed by a lawyer; the app only hosts them

name: Revenue figures for the platform admin
w: The operator needs to know whether the business is growing: monthly recurring revenue, how many trials convert and who is leaving.
ac: MRR and ARR, active, trialing, past-due and cancelled subscription counts
Trial-to-paid conversion and monthly churn
Failed payments awaiting recovery
Shown on the EP-10 metrics dashboard from admin-only functions
